calls.head: A shadow job for Mikheyev, Cirelli and Holmberg
calls.body: At home, the Lightning keep sending Cirelli’s line (Mikheyev, Cirelli and Holmberg) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jon Cooper has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Hurricanes’ first line is Carrier, Aho and Svechnikov.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Slavin’s third-period goal lifts the Hurricanes past the Lightning
paras: Anthony Cirelli opened the scoring for the Lightning on the power play just 55 seconds into the second, but they didn’t score again. The Lightning’s Pontus Holmberg left in the second period and didn’t return. Two days later, he was ruled out for four weeks with a lower-body injury. Eric Robinson tied it up for Carolina early in the third, and Jaccob Slavin put the Hurricanes ahead for good less than two minutes later. Jackson Blake added the empty-netter with 35 seconds left to make it 3-1.

Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. Brandon Bussi made 32 saves for the Hurricanes, and Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 27 of 29 at the other end. The Canes improved to 19-3-3, tied for first in the NHL in points, while the Lightning dropped to 15-7-2, second in the Atlantic.

items.text: The Hurricanes have points in eight straight games (7-0-1), the longest run in the league right now.
Jaccob Slavin scored his first goal of the season, his first since Apr 7 (25 games played since).
K'Andre Miller was in NHL.com’s projected lineup, but Juuso Välimäki played instead.
Erik Černák and Victor Hedman were in NHL.com’s projected lineup but didn’t dress.
